issue: Does a hash-value match by a private party's automated system (such as Google's) count as a private search, so that law enforcement may later view the matched file without a warrant under the private-search doctrine?

sides.position: A hash-value match is a valid private search, so law enforcement's later examination of the same file falls within the private-search doctrine and needs no warrant, because hash matching is nearly perfectly accurate and reveals nothing new.
cases: United States v. Reddick, 900 F.3d 636 (5th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Miller, 982 F.3d 412 (6th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: A hash-value match cannot constitute a valid private search, so law enforcement's examination of a matched file exceeds the private search and requires a warrant.
cases: United States v. Maher, 120 F.4th 297 (2d Cir. 2024)

quote: Our sister circuits are split over whether hash matching constitutes a valid private search.
cite: United States v. Richard Brillhart, No. 24-13232 (11th Cir. 2026)
